# New renderings — iliad-034 (5.719–813)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ἥρη πρέσβα θεὰ θυγάτηρ μεγάλοιο Κρόνοιο (5.721) | "Hera, eldest goddess, daughter of great Cronus" | "Hera, the eldest goddess, daughter of great Cronus" | "queen", "venerable", "revered" (πρέσβα keeps the table’s "eldest", 3.452; Hera calls herself the eldest child of Cronus at 4.59; the note says it is also a title of honour) |
| ἐποιχομένη χρυσάμπυκας ἔντυεν ἵππους (5.720) | "going to and fro, was making ready the gold-frontleted horses" | "went about making ready the horses with their golden frontlets" | "gold-bridled", "golden-reined"; χρυσάμπυκας keeps the English of 5.363 (iliad-030) |
| ὀκτάκνημα (κύκλα, 5.723) | "eight-spoked" | "with eight spokes" (+ note: κνήμη "shin", here "spoke") | "eight-legged", "eight-limbed" |
| καμπύλα κύκλα (5.722) | "bent wheels" | "bent wheels" | "curved wheels", "rounded wheels"; καμπύλος keeps the table’s "bent" (καμπύλον ἅρμα, 5.231; καμπύλα τόξα) |
| ἐπίσσωτρα (5.725) | "tires" | "tires" | "rims" (kept for ἴτυς), "bands", "felloes" |
| ἴτυς (5.724) | "rim" | "rim" | "felloe", "wheel-rim" (the table has "wheel-rim" at 4.486; here the part-name stands alone) |
| πλῆμναι (5.726) | "naves" | "hubs" | "bosses", "centres"; the old word "naves" kept in `l` only |
| ἄντυγες (5.728) | "rails" | "rails" | "rims", "rings"; ἄντυξ keeps the "rail" of 5.262 |
| λέπαδνα (5.730) | "yoke-straps" | "yoke-straps" (+ note: exact fitting not clear) | "breast-straps", "traces", "collars" (each decides the unknown) |
| ὠκύποδας ἵππους (5.732) | "swift-footed horses" | "swift-footed horses" | "fleet-footed"; follows the table’s ὠκύποδες |
| Ἀθηναίη κούρη Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο (5.733) | "Athena, daughter of aegis-bearing Zeus" | "Athena, daughter of aegis-bearing Zeus" | "child of Zeus"; follows Παλλὰς Ἀθηναίη κούρη Διὸς αἰγιόχοιο (3.42) |
| ἑανόν (πέπλον … ἑανόν, 5.734) | "fine" | "fine" (+ note: sense not certain, perhaps "soft" or "light") | "flowing", "soft", "filmy" (each picks a guess) |
| δακρυόεντα (πόλεμον, 5.737) | "tearful" | "tearful" | "grievous", "lamentable"; the Odyssey table has "tearful" for the same adjective in its compounds |
| θυσσανόεσσαν (αἰγίδα, 5.738) | "tasselled" | "tasselled" | "fringed", "shaggy"; keeps the "tasselled" of the glossary entry for αἰγίς |
| Φόβος · Ἔρις · Ἀλκή · Ἰωκή (the figures on the aegis, 5.739–740) | "Terror" · "Strife" · "Might" · "Onset" | "Terror" · "Strife" · "Might" · "Onset" (+ note: Ἰωκή "the rush of battle"; sense not certain) | "Rout", "Pursuit", "Flight", "Panic"; Φόβος "Terror" and Ἔρις "Strife" keep 4.440; Ἀλκή "Might" keeps ἀλκή "might"; Ἰωκή "Onset" keeps ἰωκάς "onsets", 5.521 |
| κρυόεσσα (Ἰωκή, 5.740) | "chilling" | "chilling" | "icy", "freezing", "dreadful" |
| Γοργείη κεφαλὴ δεινοῖο πελώρου (5.741) | "the Gorgon head of a dread monster" | "the Gorgon head of a dread monster" | Odyssey wording, unchanged (11.634) |
| δεινή τε σμερδνή τε (5.742) | "dread and frightful" | "dread and frightful" | "terrible and grim"; σμερδνή keeps the "frightful" of σμερδαλέος (12.91) |
| ἀμφίφαλον · τετραφάληρον (κυνέην, 5.743) | "two-ridged" · "four-ridged" | "two-ridged" · "four-ridged" (+ note: φάλος "ridge of the helmet", sense not certain) | "two-crested", "four-plated", "four-horned", "double-crested" (each decides the unknown) |
| ἑκατὸν πολίων πρυλέεσσ’ ἀραρυῖαν (5.744) | "fitted for the foot-soldiers of a hundred cities" | "fitted for the foot-soldiers of a hundred cities" (+ note: whether "suited to" or "carrying the figures of", not said) | "adorned with", "big enough for"; "foremost fighters" for πρυλέες |
| ἐς δ’ ὄχεα φλόγεα ποσὶ βήσετο (5.745) | "and onto the chariot, flaming, with her feet she stepped" | "stepped with her feet into the flaming chariot" | "fiery chariot", "blazing"; φλόγεα "flaming" |
| κεντρηνεκέας (ἵππους, 5.752) | "goad-driven" | "goad-driven" (+ note: usual explanation: κέντρον "goad" + the root "carry"; sense not known) | "goaded", "spurred on", "stinging" |
| αὐτόμαται δὲ πύλαι μύκον οὐρανοῦ ἃς ἔχον Ὧραι (5.749) | "And of themselves the gates of heaven bellowed, which the Hours kept," | "Then of their own accord the gates of heaven, which the Hours kept, bellowed," | "groaned", "creaked", "rumbled" (μυκάομαι is the lowing of cattle); Ὧραι "the Hours" (goddesses), not "the Seasons" |
| πυκινὸν νέφος (5.751) | "solid cloud" | "solid cloud" | "thick", "dense"; πυκινός keeps the house word "solid" (πυκινὸν λόχον, 4.392) |
| ἠμὲν ἀνακλῖναι … ἠδ’ ἐπιθεῖναι (5.751) | "both to open and to shut" | "both to open and to shut" | follows Odyssey 11.525; "roll back … and close" |
| ἐξείρετο καὶ προσέειπε (5.756) | "questioned and addressed" | "questioned … and spoke to him" | "asked and answered"; ἐξείρομαι "question" |
| Ζῆν’ ὕπατον Κρονίδην (5.756) | "Zeus, highest son-of-Cronus" | "Zeus, the son of Cronus, the highest one" | follows ὕπατε κρειόντων "highest of rulers" and Κρονίδης "son of Cronus" |
| οὐ νεμεσίζῃ Ἄρῃ τάδε καρτερὰ ἔργα (5.757) | "do you not feel resentment at Ares for these mighty deeds" | "do you not feel resentment at Ares for these mighty deeds" | "are you not indignant", "does it not anger you"; follows νεμεσίζομαι "I feel no resentment at" (2.296) |
| μὰψ ἀτὰρ οὐ κατὰ κόσμον (5.759) | "recklessly and not in due order" | "recklessly and not in due order" | "in vain", "at random", "wantonly"; κόσμος "order" as in the glossary |
| ἄφρονα τοῦτον ἀνέντες, ὃς οὔ τινα οἶδε θέμιστα (5.761) | "having let go this senseless one, who knows no rules of right" | "who have let this senseless creature loose, who knows no rules of right" | "mad", "reckless"; θέμιστα "rules of right" ("law" is reserved for θέμις) (plural of θέμις) |
| ἔπορσον Ἀθηναίην ἀγελείην (5.765) | "set Athena the spoil-driver on him" | "rouse Athena, the driver of spoil, against him" | "send"; Ἀθηναίη ἀγελείη keeps the table’s "the spoil-driver" / "the driver of spoil" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε θεὰ λευκώλενος Ἥρη (5.767, whole-line formula) | "So he spoke, and did not disobey, the goddess, white-armed Hera," | "So he spoke, and the goddess, white-armed Hera, did not disobey;" | the pattern of the 5.719 line (2.166) with λευκώλενος "white-armed" for γλαυκῶπις "gleaming-eyed" |
| μεσσηγὺς γαίης τε καὶ οὐρανοῦ ἀστερόεντος (5.769) | "between earth and starry heaven" | "between earth and starry heaven" | "the starry sky" is kept for ἀστερόεις οὐρανός (11.17); "bright with stars" |
| ὑψηχέες ἵπποι (5.772) | "high-sounding horses" | "high-sounding horses" (+ note: ὕψι + ἠχέω, perhaps of neighing; sense not certain) | "high-stepping", "loud-neighing", "tall" (each decides the unknown) |
| ποταμώ τε ῥέοντε · Σιμόεις · Σκάμανδρος (5.773–774) | "the two flowing rivers" · "the Simois" · "the Scamander" | "the two flowing rivers" · "the Simois" · "the Scamander" | "Simoeis"; the rivers by their usual English names |
| ἀμβροσίην Σιμόεις ἀνέτειλε νέμεσθαι (5.777) | "the Simois made ambrosia spring up to graze on" | "the Simois made ambrosia spring up to feed on" | "grow"; ἀνατέλλω causative "made spring up" |
| τρήρωσι πελειάσιν (5.778) | "timorous doves" | "timorous doves" | "shy", "trembling", "swift"; keeps the Odyssey’s "timorous" (Odyssey 12.62) |
| ἀνδράσιν Ἀργείοισιν ἀλεξέμεναι (5.779) | "to defend the Argive men" | "to defend the Argive men" | "to ward off" |
| ὠμοφάγοισιν (λείουσιν, 5.782) | "raw-eating" | "that eat raw flesh" | "flesh-eating", "ravenous", "savage" |
| Στέντορι … μεγαλήτορι χαλκεοφώνῳ (5.785) | "great-spirited Stentor, bronze-voiced" | "great-spirited Stentor of the bronze voice" | "brazen-voiced", "bronze-throated"; μεγαλήτωρ keeps "great-spirited" |
| αὐδήσασχ’ (5.786) | "called out" | "shout" | the form is printed so; the final χ’ is left unexplained in the note |
| αἰδὼς Ἀργεῖοι κάκ’ ἐλέγχεα εἶδος ἀγητοί (5.787) | "Shame, Argives, base disgraces, admirable in form!" | "Shame, Argives, you base disgraces, admirable in form!" | "fine to look at", "handsome only"; κάκ’ ἐλέγχεα keeps "base disgraces" (2.235) and ἀγητός "admirable" |
| πωλέσκετο · οἴχνεσκον (5.788–790, iterative) | "used to go into the war" · "use to go about" | "used to go to the war" · "never used to go out" | "kept going" |
| πρὸ πυλάων Δαρδανιάων (5.789) | "before the Dardanian gates" | "in front of the Dardanian gates" | "Dardan gates", "the Gates of Dardanus"; the adjective stays an adjective |
| κείνου γὰρ ἐδείδισαν ὄβριμον ἔγχος (5.790) | "for that man’s mighty spear they feared" | "for they were afraid of his mighty spear" | "dreaded his stout spear"; ὄβριμος keeps "mighty" |
| ὣς εἰποῦσ’ ὄτρυνε μένος καὶ θυμὸν ἑκάστου (5.792) | "So having spoken, she urged on the might and the heart of each man." | "So she spoke, and urged on the might and the heart of each man." | feminine of the Iliad line at 5.470 (iliad-031: "might", not the Odyssey’s "strength"); a departure from the Odyssey’s "strength" (Odyssey 33.15) |
| ἕλκος ἀναψύχοντα (5.795) | "cooling the wound" | "cooling the wound" | "airing", "drying", "letting the wound cool" |
| ἀσπίδος εὐκύκλου (5.797) | "of the shield, well-rounded" | "his well-rounded shield" | "round", "well-balanced", "fair-circled" |
| κελαινεφὲς αἷμα (5.798) | "dark-clouded blood" | "blood, dark as a cloud" | keeps the table’s αἷμα κελαινεφές (4.140, 11.36) |
| ἱππείου … ζυγοῦ (5.799) | "the yoke of the horses" | "the yoke of his horses" | "horse-yoke" |
| ἦ ὀλίγον οἷ παῖδα ἐοικότα γείνατο Τυδεύς (5.800) | "Truly a child little like himself Tydeus begot." | "Truly Tydeus fathered a son little like himself." | "no true son" |
| Τυδεύς τοι μικρὸς μὲν ἔην δέμας, ἀλλὰ μαχητής (5.801) | "Tydeus, I tell you, was small in build, but a fighter" | "Tydeus, I tell you, was small in build, but a fighter" | "was a small man" |
| οὐδ’ ἐκπαιφάσσειν (5.803) | "nor dash out" | "or dash out" | "dart about"; the sense is not fully clear |
| πολέας … Καδμείωνας (5.804) | "the many Cadmeans" | "the many Cadmeans" | "Cadmus’ sons", "Thebans"; keeps 4.385 |
| κούρους Καδμείων προκαλίζετο, πάντα δ’ ἐνίκα ῥηϊδίως (5.807–808) | "kept challenging the young men of the Cadmeans, and won at everything easily" | "kept challenging the young men of the Cadmeans, and won at everything easily" | follows 4.389–390 (iliad-025) for προκαλίζετο … πάντα δ’ ἐνίκα ῥηϊδίως |
| τοίη οἱ ἐγὼν ἐπιτάρροθος ἦα (5.808) | "such a helper to him was I" | "Such a helper was I to him" | follows τοίη οἱ ἐπίρροθος ἦεν Ἀθήνη (4.390); "helper" for ἐπιτάρροθος (24.182), a departure only in person |
| σοὶ … παρά θ’ ἵσταμαι ἠδὲ φυλάσσω (5.809) | "I stand beside you and guard you" | "I stand by you and guard you" | "watch over" |
| προφρονέως (5.810) | "readily" | "readily" | "eagerly", "with a ready heart"; keeps the Odyssey’s "ready mind" |
| κάματος πολυᾶϊξ … γυῖα δέδυκεν (5.811) | "much-darting weariness has sunk into your limbs" | "a weariness that darts upon you again and again has sunk into your limbs" (+ note: πολυ- "much" + the root of ἀΐσσω "dart"; exact force not known) | "unceasing", "pervasive", "wearing" (each decides the unknown) |
| δέος … ἀκήριον (5.812) | "fear … spiritless" | "spiritless fear" (+ note: from κῆρ "heart"; rare, sense not certain) | "heart-numbing", "deadly"; not "uninjured" (12.98 ἀκήριος, a different reading) |
| Τυδέος ἔκγονός ἐσσι δαΐφρονος Οἰνεΐδαο (5.813) | "the offspring of Tydeus, wise-minded, the son of Oeneus" | "the offspring of wise-hearted Tydeus, the son of Oeneus" | δαΐφρων keeps "wise-minded" in `l` and "wise-hearted" in `i` (4.252) |
